title: Balanced global clock tree with local clock buffers
decision: Implement a balanced global clock tree feeding local clock buffers (LCBs) that distribute clocks to sequential elements across the die
alternatives_or_rejected: A single centrally buffered clock, an unbalanced clock distribution, or a pure clock mesh without local buffering
rationale: A balanced tree provides deterministic, controllable skew across the large die; local buffers allow tuning for varying capacitive loads and enable fine-grained clock gating
outcome: Low global clock skew was maintained across the multi-core floorplan, supporting high-frequency operation

title: Mixed static and dynamic circuit families
decision: Use dynamic domino logic for performance-critical datapaths (floating-point units, register files, cache arrays) and static CMOS for control and irregular logic
alternatives_or_rejected: Using only static CMOS throughout the design, or using only dynamic logic everywhere
rationale: Dynamic circuits deliver higher speed and smaller area for wide, regular datapath functions, while static CMOS offers better noise immunity and design productivity for irregular control logic
outcome: Frequency targets were met in the datapaths, while control logic remained robust and manageable to design

title: Hierarchical timing closure with macro budgets
decision: Adopt a hierarchical static timing closure flow in which individual macros and units were timed to agreed interface budgets, rather than performing flat full-chip timing
alternatives_or_rejected: Flat static timing analysis across the entire 170-million-transistor chip
rationale: Flat timing on a design of this size was computationally prohibitive and would have serialized the design process; hierarchical budgets enabled parallel macro development and faster iteration
outcome: Timing closure was achieved within the design schedule, with full-chip verification used as a final sign-off step

title: Full-custom macros for regular structures
decision: Employ full-custom design for regular, performance-critical macros such as caches, register files, and datapaths, while using standard-cell and semi-custom flows for control logic
alternatives_or_rejected: A purely standard-cell ASIC methodology for the entire chip, or full-custom design for all logic including irregular control blocks
rationale: Full-custom layout achieves maximum density, performance, and bit-line symmetry for regular array structures; standard-cell tools are far more efficient for the irregular control logic that dominates by instance count
outcome: Optimal area and performance for arrays and datapaths, with manageable design effort and schedule for control logic
